title: chainbench DSL v2
description: Canonical grammar for v2 spec files (docs/dev/dsl-v2-proposal.md). Enforcement is the strict parser (internal/dsl/spec_v2.go); this document is the field-level source of truth the parser and docs must match.

description.description: Prose saying what this document is for. No execution semantics.

manifest.description: an external, project-supplied chain manifest JSON run on the family named by chain (the DSL equivalent of --manifest)

genesisTemplate.description: the genesis template for manifest (the DSL equivalent of --genesis-template)

binaries.description: name -> binary path. "default" applies to every node without its own; a per-node topology entry's "binary" names one of these; an upgrade names "from"/"to"

blueprint.description: a network declaration file — the layout and the node keys in one document (the DSL equivalent of --blueprint); with it no topology or key set is needed

mode.description: existing | build | inherit are designed but have no runtime seam yet; the parser rejects them by name

set.description: dot-path single values merged into the overlay

topology.description: either the count form ({bp, en, pn, syncMode}) or the node table ({nodes: [{role, binary, sync, bootnode, index}]}); the node table gives each node its own role and binary

launch.description: scope -> launchopt knobs. scope: "all", a role (bp, en, pn), or "node<N>"; applied per node most-general-first (all, then role, then node)

config.description: scope -> config-knob overrides. scope: "all", a role (bp, en, pn), or "node<N>"; applied per node most-general-first (all, then role, then node)

upgrade.description: a hardfork crossing. A concurrent handoff starts on binaries.from and forks to binaries.to, shaped by a preset under presets/chain; a restart crosses one chain's own fork on one binary at a time and names the fork itself.

preset.description: a hardfork preset under presets/chain, without the directory or the .yaml extension

fork.description: which fork is crossed. Required for a restart; for a handoff the preset answers, and a repetition that disagrees is refused.

at.description: the block the fork activates at. Required for a restart; for a handoff the preset answers.

from.description: the binaries entry the network starts on (default "from")

to.description: the binaries entry it ends on (default "to")

style.description: concurrent: two builds run side by side across the fork. restart: one build at a time, every node relaunched on the successor.

carry.description: where the successor reads the fork settings from

accounts.description: Test accounts created and funded when the network is up. Declared here rather than in the genesis so adding or renaming one does not force a new genesis and a re-init of every datadir.

fund.description: Balance to send once the chain is sealing, in wei (decimal or 0x-hex). Omit for an account that must start at zero — what a test needs to exercise the paths that fail for want of gas.

attach.description: Run against a network that is already up instead of composing one. Exclusive with every field that describes a network to build.

rpc.description: Node RPC endpoints, in the order node selectors address them. ${VAR:-default} is expanded.

keysDir.description: Key set the running network was composed from, so a spec can name an account by label.

provides.description: What the running network offers, for capability-gated cases. Not "capabilities", which is a requirement.

validators.description: how many of a generated set join the validator set (0 = all; generate only)

description.description: Prose saying what this document is for. No execution semantics.

oneOf.description: env id resolved against the case file's directory

timeouts.description: per-case timeout budgets. Only case (alias test) is read — the interpreter bounds the whole case with it — so the parser refuses any other name rather than validating a duration that nothing applies.

steps.description: unified sequence; at least one expect statement is required

expect.description: adjunct on a do statement: the outcome the step must reach. receipt = mined, revert = mined with status 0x0, reject = the submit itself must fail, fail = a launched node must not come up. The parser refuses anything else (dsl.expectAdjuncts), because a typo would otherwise fall through to the default "must succeed" and turn a negative case positive.
